kind: ThreadSanitizer run for the two runtime/thread.rs free_lock rows

reviewer.note: the instrument was derived from forensics/tools/ms_tsan.py's own recipe, not re-invented; where it differs from that tool the difference is stated

subject.identity_note: both definition hashes and the set hash were recomputed from the S blob with the tool's documented normalisation (splitlines, rstrip each line, join with \n, sha256 over UTF-8, no trailing newline) and equal the values in evidence/closure-ssh-b80b.json
subject.ledger_observation: the two rows share one stable id: they are one operation with two cfg-exclusive definitions, recorded as two obligations. Not a soundness defect, but the ledger double-counts the operation.

instrument.rustup_home: court/freeze-b80/review7/.phase25-rustup (the date-pinned toolchain installed for this run)
instrument.identity_deviation: forensics/tools/ms_tsan.py pins NIGHTLY_HOME=/work/.phase25-rustup; this review was confined to court/freeze-b80/review7/**, so the same pinned nightly and the same component were installed under review7 instead. Same channel date and same rustc commit hash, different install path.
instrument.std_instrumentation: std is rebuilt under TSan (-Zbuild-std), which matters here: RwlockInner is `{ state: Mutex<LockState>, cond: Condvar }`, so the happens-before edges this lock relies on live inside std. A crate-only instrumentation would not see them and its result would be neither a pass nor a useful failure.
instrument.shadow_mapping: the TSan binary mapped its shadow and ran; the container's per-process RLIMIT_DATA is `unlimited`, so the OPENSSL_RS_COURT_DATA venue override documented in ms_tsan.py was not needed in this container

venue.change: docker update --memory 16g --memory-swap 16g --memory-reservation 16g (the standing venue directive for this campaign; the 8 GiB cap was the state the container was found in)
venue.parallelism: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 (AGENTS.md §6.1 rule 4); one heavy command at a time; nothing else compiled during any run
venue.baseline_build: the stable 1.98.1 test binary was already warm (0.03 s), so the stable runs below recompiled nothing

includes: tests::lock_hook::hook_observes_authority_size_and_single_release (spawns a child process that frees the block and asserts the allocator hook saw exactly one release at the authority size)

coverage.note: the dedicated release-side probe: alloc -> use -> free, one process per probe

includes: the exhaustive scheduler model and its three mutants

canaries.meaning: the instrument, and its shadow, are live in this venue
TSan detects the defect class a release side carries (a 56-byte block, the authority RwLock size, freed while a second thread reads it through a happens-before edge), not only plain data races

results.statement: no ThreadSanitizer report on any of the runs above, on either schedule. The two free_lock rows therefore no longer lack the instrument the b80 argument named: TSan ran at S against the lock, refcount, rcu and store-refcount surfaces, with firing canaries on both the race and the release class.
results.state_after: ESTABLISHED-AT-INSTRUMENT-LEVEL for the observed schedules: the release side of the primitive executes in this instrument without a race or a use-after-free report. This is not §7 SAFETY_DISCHARGED: the caller precondition ('exclusively owned by this call') is not something TSan can establish, because no test performs the forbidden shape.

instrument_defects_found.statement: the b79/b80 contract control C3a_contract_present reports both free_lock rows as `no-fn-level-#Safety`; both definitions carry a complete `# Safety`. C3a's upward scan stops at `))]`, so a multi-line `#[cfg(all(...))]` attribute between the doc comment and the `fn` hides the contract. Demonstrated with the additive check C3a2 in court/freeze-b80/review7/ctrl_rest_at_S.py, which passes all 48 rows. Recorded as G3 in evidence/b80-review-drifted.json.

loom.available: yes: `loom = "0.7"` is a `[target.'cfg(loom)'.dev-dependencies]` entry in Cargo.toml
loom.existing_use: four `loom::model` tests in src/runtime/refcount.rs (lines ~736-871) over the refcount protocol
loom.fit_for_the_free_side: poor. loom models its own atomics/Arc and detects races, deadlocks and ordering violations; it does not model freeing a non-loom allocation, so it cannot express 'the block is released while a waiter still holds it'. TSan (or Miri's provenance checking) is the instrument for this side.
loom.proposed_batch: B81-P1 (proposal only, NOT made here): add a `cfg(loom)` test for the LockState transitions (read/write/unlock, the read->write refusal and the per-thread accounting) beside the existing refcount loom tests, and a focused `--ignored` probe that frees a lock immediately after its last holder while a second thread is inside a failed acquire, so the release window is executed deliberately rather than incidentally.

residuals.statement: no test performs the shape the precondition forbids (a free while another thread still uses the lock), so the clean TSan result cannot establish that precondition; it establishes that every executed release path is race- and UAF-free
only the linux/x86_64/gnu/64-bit definition is compiled and executed; the `Box` alternative (off the measured profile) is not compiled in this build, so TSan says nothing about it
a clean TSan run bounds the executed schedules only; a race not observed is not a race absent
no Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows) or ASan/LSan run covers the release side; no loom model covers the lock
the full library suite was not run under TSan (2378 tests); the surface chosen is the concurrency-bearing one (thread, refcount, rcu, store refcount)
the ledger records this one operation as two obligations (same stable id, two cfg-exclusive definitions)

does_not_prove: that the two free_lock rows are §7 SAFETY_DISCHARGED: the caller's exclusive-ownership obligation is a contract obligation, and TSan cannot establish it
that the crate is race-free: only the listed filters ran, on the two recorded schedules
that `CRYPTO_THREAD_lock_free` is never called concurrently with a user by any consumer (ssh/sshd/curl): that is a caller audit, not an instrument result
anything about the off-profile `Box` definition, memory ordering at the intrinsics level, or cryptographic/timing properties
that the third-party TSan runtime itself is bug-free; the two canaries only show it fires on the two classes tested
